key_insight: SpyCAT is a semi-supervised, spatially context-aware transformer that models "normal" brain MRI patches to detect subtle epileptogenic lesions as anomalies.
clinical_relevance: It may help localize small, hard-to-see lesions in 3D brain MRI, supporting more reliable lesion detection for epilepsy workups.
method: Patch-based transformer fed by discrete tokens from a vector-quantizing variational autoencoder
Uses full 3D convolutions to generate counterfactual patches and encode spatial context
Built as a modeling-based anomaly detector with explicit assumptions about normal vs abnormal tissue
evidence_signal: In point-annotated evaluations of two epileptogenic lesion subtypes, SpyCAT reportedly performed well and outperformed state-of-the-art reference methods using Metrics Reloaded-based measures.
watch_item: Performance is shown on specific lesion subtypes with point annotations, so broader generalization and real-world deployment need further validation.
paper_title: Spatially Context-Aware Transformers Facilitate Modeling-Based Anomaly Detection of Subtle Lesions in Brain MRI Images
